title: The state of short-term rental operations 2027: turnovers, tasks, phones, messages and reviews
summary: A year of STR operations data: same-day turnovers, clean times, maintenance by season, night calls, message timing and review responses.
body_markdown:
**What does running short-term rentals actually look like, measured rather than guessed? We looked at a year of operations on ProhostAI: about 400,000 checkouts, 31,000 timed turnover cleans, 217,000 tasks, 6,800 phone calls and 147,000 reviews. Half of all checkouts are same-day turnovers. A turnover clean takes about two hours. Most tasks start as a guest message. Night calls are rare but are mostly about getting in. And only 1 in 8 reviews gets a public response from the host.**


## Key takeaways


- **Turnovers:** **49%** of checkouts are same-day turnovers. The median turnover clean takes **120 minutes** ; **1 in 6** same-day cleans finishes after the next guest's check-in time.
- **Tasks:** **58%** of tasks were created by AI, mostly from guest messages and reviews. General maintenance, guest requests and early check-in requests are the three biggest categories.
- **Seasons:** heating and cooling, pest and outdoor issues take a bigger share of repairs in summer; pool and hot tub issues peak in spring; plumbing is steady all year.
- **Phones:** only **4.9%** of inbound calls come between 10pm and 7am, but calls after 6pm are about **twice as likely** to be about getting into the property.
- **Messages:** the typical welcome message goes out **2 minutes** after booking, the check-in message about **24 hours** before check-in, and the checkout message about **18 hours** before checkout.
- **Reviews:** **11.8%** of reviews get a public host response (about 1 in 8), and about half of businesses never respond. On 1 to 3 star reviews, **value, accuracy and cleanliness** are the lowest sub-scores.

## Where we're coming from


I spent 6 years at Airbnb as a staff data scientist on the hosting team, and we host in Hawaii, the Smokies and Joshua Tree. This report pulls together the operations studies we published this month into one place, with each chapter's method stated next to its numbers. It's the report I wanted when I started hosting: what normal looks like, so you can tell when your own numbers aren't.


> **How we measured it.** All numbers come from ProhostAI's production data, read as aggregates only. We never look at individual guests or businesses for this report, internal and test workspaces are excluded, and every published number has at least 5 businesses and at least 30 listings behind it (or at least 30 records where the unit isn't a listing). Times use each property's local time zone, which matters for Hawaii, two to three hours behind the West Coast. Each chapter states its own window and sample. Where one business makes up a large share of a sample, we re-ran the numbers without it and say so. The data reflects businesses that use ProhostAI, which skew toward professional hosts and property managers in the US.


## Chapter 1: Turnovers


**Sample:** 30,985 turnover cleans timed in the app (start to finish, 10 minutes to 12 hours) at 146 businesses and 2,249 listings; 398,510 confirmed checkouts at 12,556 listings and 843 businesses. November 19, 2025 to November 19, 2026.


Bedrooms Median clean Slowest 10% start at Same-day turnover share


Studio or 1 85 min 206 min 55.8%


2 106 min 248 min 51.1%


3 146 min 310 min 44.3%


4 165 min 335 min 38.1%


5+ 201 min 363 min 34.1%


**All** **120 min** **294 min** **49.0%**


On same-day turnovers, the median window between checkout time and the next check-in time is **5 hours** . Cleaners start a median **63 minutes** after checkout, finish in **111 minutes** , and have **94 minutes** to spare. **82%** finish before the next check-in time.


**What to do:** plan from the median, buffer to the slowest quarter, and treat every same-day turnover as a deadline. The full breakdown and a copyable playbook:[How long does a turnover clean take?](https://prohost.ai/blog/turnover-cleaning-time-benchmarks)


## Chapter 2: What breaks, and when


**Sample:** 216,915 tasks created November 1, 2025 to November 1, 2026, of which 150,311 were unscheduled tasks tied to a listing, at 695 businesses. Seasonal tables use northern-hemisphere listings only.


Who created the task Share


AI, from a guest message or review, or an AI employee 57.6%


Recurring and booking-triggered schedules 29.9%


A person 10.4%


Other (API, automated alerts) 2.1%


The biggest unscheduled categories: general maintenance **17.5%** , guest requests **14.0%** , early check-in **11.1%** , cleanliness **8.1%** , access issues **7.8%** , booking help **5.9%** , late checkout **4.9%** and plumbing **4.0%** .


Share of repair tasks Winter Spring Summer Fall


Plumbing 11.8% 9.9% 11.5% 13.0%


Heating and cooling 8.2% 5.4% 9.2% 7.8%


Pool, hot tub, spa 7.4% 9.4% 6.0% 5.8%


Pest control 4.0% 3.9% 5.9% 4.9%


**What to do:** service each system before its season, and make sure a guest's complaint becomes a task without someone retyping it. Full tables and a maintenance calendar:[Vacation rental maintenance issues by season](https://prohost.ai/blog/vacation-rental-maintenance-issues-by-season)


## Chapter 3: The phone at night


**Sample:** 6,796 inbound calls to 41 businesses' phone lines (1,890 listings), May 23 to November 18, 2026. Topics come from keyword matches on each call's AI summary.


Day (7am to 6pm) Evening (6pm to 10pm) Night (10pm to 7am)


Share of all calls 82.7% 12.5% 4.9%


Calls about getting in 8.7% 17.8% 16.5%


Calls about something broken 7.8% 10.3% 11.8%


Calls that never connected 12.5% 10.9% 15.8%


The median answered call lasted **60 seconds** .


**What to do:** write an after-hours plan that answers access and how-to questions without waking anyone, and lists the few emergencies that do. Full study and a copyable plan:[What guests call about at night](https://prohost.ai/blog/what-guests-call-about-at-night)


## Chapter 4: When hosts message guests


**Sample:** automated messages ProhostAI actually sent for confirmed reservations, November 19, 2025 to November 19, 2026: 18,559 welcome messages at 70 businesses (sent within a week of booking), 22,191 check-in messages at 85 businesses and 13,076 checkout messages at 50 businesses (each sent in the 7 days before check-in or checkout). Timing is measured from the booking time and from each reservation's check-in or checkout time.


Message Median timing Middle half of messages


Welcome (booking confirmed) 2 minutes after booking 1 to 5 minutes after


Check-in 24 hours before check-in time 48 hours to 3 hours before


Checkout about 18 hours before checkout time 24 to 15 hours before


Check-in timing is the most spread out: a quarter of check-in messages go out **in the last 3 hours** before check-in, and a quarter **2 or more days** ahead. Many hosts also send a message after arrival; those aren't in the table, which only counts messages sent before check-in. Checkout messages are tighter: the middle half go out 15 to 24 hours before checkout, which for a 10am or 11am checkout means the afternoon or evening before.


**What to do:** welcome right away, send the details that need planning (parking, directions) two or three days out, send the door code on arrival day, and send checkout instructions the evening before. Wording for each:[Airbnb message templates](https://prohost.ai/blog/airbnb-message-templates)


## Chapter 5: Reviews


**Sample:** 147,423 guest reviews published November 19, 2025 to November 19, 2026. A "response" is a public host response that the channel reports back. The sub-scores in the table come from the 135,352 of those reviews on a 5-star scale, at 9,127 listings and 729 businesses; reviews on a 10-point scale (Booking.com-style) don't carry the same sub-scores, and almost none of them have a host response, which is why the response rate on 5-star-scale reviews alone runs a little higher.


Stars Reviews Value Accuracy Cleanliness Communication Check-in Location


1 to 3 6,134 2.54 2.98 3.00 3.54 3.68 3.66


4 12,705 4.18 4.39 4.27 4.66 4.59 4.53


5 116,513 4.90 4.96 4.92 4.97 4.95 4.92


**All** **135,352** 4.73 4.82 4.78 4.88 4.86 4.83


Two findings stand out. First, bad reviews get a response about as often as good ones, even though a bad review is the one the next guest reads most closely. Among the 484 businesses with at least 30 reviews, **51%** never responded to any, and only **5%** responded to half or more. Second, when a stay goes wrong, guests mark down **value, accuracy and cleanliness** the hardest, while communication and check-in hold up better. A bad review is usually about the home and the price, not the host's messages.


**What to do:** respond to every review under 4 stars, briefly and specifically, for the next guest reading it. Fix the cleanliness and accuracy gaps first: clean to a[checklist](https://prohost.ai/blog/airbnb-cleaning-checklist) and make the listing match the home. More:[How to get more 5-star reviews](https://prohost.ai/blog/how-to-get-more-5-star-reviews) and[How to remove an Airbnb review](https://prohost.ai/blog/how-to-remove-airbnb-review) .

## FAQ


### What percentage of Airbnb checkouts are same-day turnovers?


In our data, 49% of confirmed checkouts were followed by a check-in at the same listing on the same day: 56% for studios and one-bedrooms, 34% for homes with five or more bedrooms.


### How long does a vacation rental turnover take?


The median timed turnover clean took 120 minutes, from about 85 minutes for a studio or one-bedroom to about 200 for five bedrooms or more.


### How many hosts respond to their reviews?


11.8% of the 147,423 reviews in our data had a public host response, about 1 in 8, and 51% of businesses with at least 30 reviews never responded to any.


### When should I send the check-in message?


Among check-in messages ProhostAI sent in the week before arrival, the median went out 24 hours before check-in time; a quarter went out in the last 3 hours and a quarter 2 or more days ahead. A common pattern is logistics a few days early and the door code on the day.


### Is this data representative of all hosts?


No. It covers businesses that use ProhostAI, which skew toward professional hosts and property managers, mostly in the US. We state each sample so you can judge how close it is to your own business.


## The takeaway


Normal, in numbers: half your checkouts are same-day turnovers, a clean takes about two hours, most issues start as a guest message, the phone is quiet at night except for people who can't get in, and almost nobody answers their bad reviews. Each of those is something you can plan for. Start with the one that cost you the most this year.
